# Decks

*Describes silverpoint 0.9.1.*

A deck is Marp Markdown that renders as silverpoint slides: the `silverpoint` theme, its grounds and
substrates as directives, and real charts from `silverpoint` fences. `SpDeck` renders it in React, Vue
and Angular, on the server and in the browser, with a keyboard-driven controller.

|  | React | Vue | Angular | Reflex |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Name | `SpDeck` | `SpDeck` | `sp-deck` | — |
| Import | `@silverpoint/react/deck` | `@silverpoint/vue/deck` | `@silverpoint/angular/deck` | — |

Optional peer of the adapters: `@silverpoint/marp`, which carries the engine and Marpit. Reflex has no deck until `reflex-silverpoint-marp` ships.

Install the peer beside the adapter:

```sh
npm install @silverpoint/marp@0.9.1
```

Import the stylesheets in this order: `@silverpoint/fonts/fonts.css`, `@silverpoint/grounds/styles.css`, `@silverpoint/grounds/ui.css`, `@silverpoint/marp/deck.css`. React and Vue import them in
the entry file. Angular lists them in the `styles` array of `angular.json`.

## Authoring

Slides are separated by `---` on a line of its own. The front matter sets the deck's directives. A
comment holding `key: value` sets a directive from that slide on, and the `_key` spot form sets it on
that slide only. Any other comment is a speaker note, shown under the slide when `showNotes` is on.

~~~markdown
---
ground: silverpoint
substrate: cream
paginate: true
footer: Quarterly review
---

<!-- _class: lead -->

# Quarterly review

The third quarter, in four slides.

---

## What changed

* Direct visits grew
* Search fell back
* Referrals held

<!-- Pause on the second point. -->
~~~

- Each list item is a **fragment**: the deck reveals them one step at a time. Print and a static
  render show every fragment.
- Headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, blockquotes, inline and block code, and images are styled by
  the theme. Code is set in EB Garamond with tabular figures, on a framed plate: there is no
  monospace.
- **Raw HTML is never rendered**: it shows as text. `javascript:` and non-image `data:` URLs are
  dropped. Do not reach for HTML to lay out a slide; use the classes and Marpit's image syntax.
- Marpit's image syntax works: `![bg](photo.jpg)`, split backgrounds (`![bg right:40%](photo.jpg)`),
  sizing and filters. The generated backdrop sits under them.
- Marpit's own directives keep their meaning: `theme`, `class`, `paginate`, `header`, `footer`,
  `backgroundColor`, `backgroundImage`, `color`, `size`, `headingDivider`, `lang`.
- A deck holds at most 512 KB, 300 slides and 60 chart fences. Past a limit it renders up to it and
  warns `SP029`.

## Directives

| Directive | Values | Default | Spot form | Written as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ground` | `silverpoint`, `cyanotype` | `silverpoint` | `_ground` | `data-sp-ground` |
| `substrate` | one of the slide's ground's substrates: `silverpoint` `cream`, `green`, `blue`, `ochre`; `cyanotype` `prussian` | `cream` | `_substrate` | `data-sp-substrate` |
| `mode` | `ink`, `precision` | `ink` | `_mode` | `data-sp-mode` |

A chart fence takes its slide's `ground`, `substrate` and `mode` unless its spec names its own. An
unknown value, or a substrate of another ground, warns `SP027` with the closest names and keeps the
inherited value.

~~~markdown
---
ground: silverpoint
---

# On cream paper

---

<!-- _ground: cyanotype -->
<!-- _mode: precision -->

# One slide in cyanotype, drawn with exact strokes

---

# Back on silverpoint
~~~

## Classes

Set with Marpit's `class` directive, or `_class` for one slide.

| Class | Effect |
|---|---|
| `lead` | A title slide: the content centred, the heading larger, one rule under it. |
| `invert` | Light text on the substrate darkened to the ground's ink; its contrast is computed per ground. |
| `plate` | An inked plate mark, a double rule inset from the edge, drawn behind the content. |
| `hatched` | An inked hatched band around the slide, drawn behind the content. |

~~~markdown
<!-- _class: plate -->

## A slide inside a plate mark

---

<!-- _class: hatched -->

## A slide with a hatched border

---

<!-- _class: invert -->

## A dark slide
~~~

## The chart fence

A fenced block whose info string is `silverpoint` holds one chart, as JSON: the input of the MCP
`render_chart` tool. The chart is drawn as static SVG where the fence was, and the deck hydrates it in
the browser, so it answers the pointer and the keys like any chart.

| Key | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `chart` | yes | The chart's catalog slug, such as `bar-chart`. |
| `data` |  | What the chart reads; its demo dataset when absent. |
| `props` |  | The chart's own props and the common view props; not the fence's own fields. |
| `width` |  | Width in canvas pixels; the slide's content width when absent. |
| `height` |  | Height in canvas pixels. Default `360`. |
| `id` |  | The chart's id; `<deck>-s<slide>-c<ordinal>` when absent. |
| `ground` |  | The chart's ground; the slide's when absent. |
| `substrate` |  | The chart's substrate; the slide's when absent. |
| `mode` |  | `ink` or `precision`; the slide's when absent. |
| `palette` |  | A preset's name or a palette object. |

~~~markdown
## Visits by quarter

```silverpoint
{"chart":"bar-chart","props":{"title":"Visits by quarter"},"height":400}
```
~~~

- `data` is what the chart reads, in the shape its reference names. Without it the chart draws its
  demo dataset: give real data in a real deck.
- `props` holds the chart's own props and the common view props. The fence's own keys (`data`,
  `width`, `height`, `id`, `ground`, `substrate`, `mode`, `palette`) go at the top level.
- A fence that is not JSON, names an unknown chart or prop, or asks for a size out of range draws a
  visible error figure in its place, warns `SP026` with the closest names, and leaves every other slide
  as it was.
- Inside a hydrated chart, the chart's keys win: the arrows move through its marks, not the deck.

## SpDeck

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `markdown` | `string` |  | **Required.** The Marp Markdown: front matter, `---` between slides, `silverpoint` fences for charts. |
| `page` | `number` |  | Controlled current page (1-based); pair it with `onPageChange`. |
| `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` | Uncontrolled initial page (1-based). Default `1`. |
| `id` | `string` |  | The deck's id, which scopes its CSS and names its charts; the adapter's hydration-safe id by default. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the deck region; the first heading of slide 1 by default. |
| `theme` | `string` | `'silverpoint'` | The Marpit theme. Default `'silverpoint'`. |
| `ground` | `string` | `'silverpoint'` | The deck's ground, which a `ground` directive overrides per slide. Default `'silverpoint'`. |
| `substrate` | `string` |  | The deck's substrate; the ground's first by default. |
| `mode` | `DeckMode` | `'ink'` | `ink` or `precision`, which a `mode` directive overrides per slide. Default `'ink'`. |
| `palette` | `string` |  | A palette preset's name, for the fence charts (REQ-609). |
| `size` | `DeckSize` | `'16:9'` | The slide size. Default `'16:9'`. |
| `showNotes` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the current slide's notes (Marpit comments). Default `false`. |
| `showControls` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the controls: previous, next, overview, notes, full screen. Default `true`. |
| `keyboard` | `boolean` | `true` | Handle the keys while focus is in the deck (API delta §7.3). Default `true`. |
| `swipe` | `boolean` | `true` | A horizontal swipe moves the deck. Default `true`. |
| `hash` | `boolean` | `false` | Read and write a `#<n>` deep link (REQ-602). Default `false`. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` | `true` | Hydrate the fence charts (REQ-594). Default `true`. |

The page is 1-based. Bind `page` to the host's state and listen to `pageChange`, or give `defaultPage`
and let the deck hold it. A re-render with fewer slides clamps the page and reports it through
`pageChange`.

| Event | Payload | React | Vue | Angular | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pageChange` | `{ readonly page: number; readonly total: number }` | `onPageChange` | `@page-change` | `(pageChange)` | The current page changed, by the reader or by a re-render that clamped it. |
| `fragmentChange` | `{ readonly page: number; readonly step: number; readonly steps: number }` | `onFragmentChange` | `@fragment-change` | `(fragmentChange)` | A fragment of the current slide was revealed or hidden: `step` of `steps`. |
| `ready` | `{ readonly total: number }` | `onReady` | `@ready` | `(ready)` | The deck rendered with a new slide count. |

**Keys** (while focus is in the deck): `ArrowRight`, `ArrowDown`, `PageDown`, `Space`, `Enter` go to
the next step; `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowUp`, `PageUp`, `Shift+Space` go back; `Home` and `End` jump to the
first and last slide; `o` toggles the overview, `f` full screen, `n` the notes. Keys typed into a form
field are left alone.

### Example

The Markdown is kept verbatim in a template literal. In a real app, keep the deck in a `.md` file and
load it as a string (Vite: `import markdown from './deck.md?raw'`).

```tsx
import '@silverpoint/fonts/fonts.css';
import '@silverpoint/grounds/styles.css';
import '@silverpoint/grounds/ui.css';
import '@silverpoint/marp/deck.css';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { SpDeck } from '@silverpoint/react/deck';

const MARKDOWN = `---
paginate: true
---

<!-- _class: lead -->

# Quarterly review

---

## Next steps

* Ship the deck
* Measure it`;

export function DeckView() {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  return (
    <SpDeck
      markdown={MARKDOWN}
      page={page}
      onPageChange={({ page }) => setPage(page)}
      hash={true}
    />
  );
}
```

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import '@silverpoint/fonts/fonts.css';
import '@silverpoint/grounds/styles.css';
import '@silverpoint/grounds/ui.css';
import '@silverpoint/marp/deck.css';
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { SpDeck } from '@silverpoint/vue/deck';

const markdown = `---
paginate: true
---

<!-- _class: lead -->

# Quarterly review

---

## Next steps

* Ship the deck
* Measure it`;
const page = ref(1);
</script>

<template>
  <SpDeck
    :markdown="markdown"
    v-model:page="page"
    :hash="true"
  />
</template>
```

```ts angular
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { SpDeckComponent } from '@silverpoint/angular/deck';

const MARKDOWN = `---
paginate: true
---

<!-- _class: lead -->

# Quarterly review

---

## Next steps

* Ship the deck
* Measure it`;

/** Add '@silverpoint/fonts/fonts.css', '@silverpoint/grounds/styles.css', '@silverpoint/grounds/ui.css', '@silverpoint/marp/deck.css' to the `styles` of angular.json. */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-deck-view',
  imports: [SpDeckComponent],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <sp-deck
      [markdown]="markdown"
      [page]="page()"
      (pageChange)="page.set($event.page)"
      [hash]="true"
    />
  `,
})
export class DeckView {
  protected readonly markdown = MARKDOWN;
  protected readonly page = signal(1);
}
```

### Server rendering

`SpDeck` renders the slides and their charts as markup on the server, so the first paint already shows
the deck; the browser adds the controller and hydrates the charts. In the Next.js App Router, a
component holding the page in state needs `'use client'`. With `interactive: false` the charts stay
static SVG. Print shows every slide at its own size, every fragment shown, the controls hidden.

## Agents

With the silverpoint MCP server connected, call `validate_deck` on the Markdown before you hand it
over: it reports each problem with its slide and fence. `render_deck` returns the deck, or one slide,
as a standalone HTML document. `generate_code` with `target: { deck: { markdown } }` writes the
`SpDeck` code. The `silverpoint://deck` resource is this reference's data.

| Code | Severity | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SP018` | warn | the component has no accessible name: no text content and no `label` | Give it visible text, or a `label` for an icon-only control |
| `SP026` | warn | a chart fence is invalid (its JSON, its chart, a prop, a size, or an error of the chart); the slide shows the error in its place | Fix the fence: a JSON object whose `chart` is a catalog slug, with props the chart declares |
| `SP027` | warn | a deck directive has an unknown value; the inherited value holds | Use a registered ground, one of its substrates, and `ink` or `precision` |
| `SP028` | warn | the page is outside the deck; it was clamped to the nearest slide | Keep `page` and `defaultPage` between 1 and the number of slides |
| `SP029` | warn | the Markdown exceeds a deck limit; it was rendered up to the limit | Keep a deck under 512 KB, 300 slides and 60 chart fences |

## Marp CLI and VS Code

The theme also ships as a plain stylesheet, `@silverpoint/marp/theme.css`, carrying both grounds.

```sh
npx @marp-team/marp-cli --theme node_modules/@silverpoint/marp/theme.css deck.md
```

In the Marp VS Code extension, add the file to the `markdown.marp.themes` setting. There, and in Marp
CLI with `--theme`, some things degrade: there are no generated backdrops (`plate` and `hatched` show
no ink), a `silverpoint` fence shows as code, and there is no controller.

Marp CLI with the deck's own engine renders the directives, the backdrops and the fences as static
SVG:

```sh
npx @marp-team/marp-cli --engine @silverpoint/marp/cli deck.md
```
